result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in 103 seconds on one thread with a peak of 1.45 to 1.53 GB, and reproduces every target except two Wilcoxon p-values. Two runs of the finished script (md5 c11e3c99f8dcd8a3a4f45447a324f9b5, 725 lines) gave byte-identical CSV files.

The two departures are a matter of method. The issue text quotes p = 0.007 (all libraries) and 0.012 (without zr3534_4), which are normal approximations; the exact test gives 0.005 and 0.010. The same paragraph quotes the exact value for the heat cohort (0.008), so it mixed the two methods. The script writes both for every comparison.

Three findings go beyond the targets and change how I-09 should read:
- **Cohort is associated with the excess.** The Fisher test on the 13 carriers gives p = 0.19, as in the issue. Under a stricter rule (all 54 CpGs at the cutoff: 1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012. As a continuous quantity the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). Ploidy shows nothing (p = 0.39, 1, 0.56, 0.70).
- **The excess is in every library.** All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.31 to 32 times); the 9 "without the excess" are at 1.31 to 4.83.
- **The block is not simply single-copy.** Counting all 3,570 30-mers, 2,471 (69.2%) occur once and 874 exactly twice. Of the second copies, 868 lie in three places on other linkage groups, none of which reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times in the reference.

The script also checks its inputs against each other and stops on any mismatch. It recomputes each library's median, cutoff and number of CpGs at the cutoff from the raw file, rebuilds the normalized counts of the united table from the raw counts (which fixes the library order), and confirms that its pooled differences equal step 05's meth.diff to 1e-8. Independent cross-checks agree: awk on two raw files, a Python reading of the reference, pwilcox and dhyper by hand, and all 176 per-library and 54 per-CpG values of the verifying agent's tables.

Nothing outside `06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563*` was edited. An early snapshot of the script was committed by the parent session (40cd66d, "unreviewed"); the working-tree file is the finished one.

design_decisions: The DML region is read from step 07 (dml_regions_legacy.csv, largest run of ploidy DML), so its coordinates are not typed in. This adds a dependency on step 07 beyond the step 05 tables. The script stops if that run is not on NC_047563.1.
The window is the DML region plus 10 kb on either side (39623323 to 39645520), close to the suggested 39,625,000 to 39,645,000. The script stops if the block and its 5 kb flanks do not fit.

Block rule: a CpG has excess coverage when at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff; such CpGs within 1 kb form a run; the block is the run that holds the DML region. I chose the cutoff because it is the criterion by which corrected mode removes a CpG, not to match the target.

Carrier rule: at least one tested CpG of the region at or above the library's cutoff. Because the Fisher result for cohort depends on the rule, the script also reports a stricter rule (every CpG at the cutoff) and Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess, on two scales.

Per-library medians over a zone use only the CpG sites with reads in that library, as the library median does. In the per-CpG profile a library without reads counts as 0. Both are stated in the header.
Coverage relative to the cutoff is written per library as a ratio and per CpG as the number of libraries at or above the cutoff, not as a per-CpG ratio.

Leave-one-out applies the difference rule only, as instructed, and the output says each count is therefore the largest possible number of DML. I added one row for the 9 libraries without the excess taken alone.
Wilcoxon tests are exact, with the normal approximation written beside each for part d. The script stops if two libraries tie on percent methylation.

Part f counts all 3,570 30-mers of the block, not only the sample of 60, which is kept for comparison. It also reports where the second copies of the two-copy 30-mers lie and whether any library reaches its cutoff there. The latter costs no second pass: the first pass keeps every position at or above the cutoff.

The summary has four columns (section, quantity, value, how_defined), one more than specified. Values are text: a number, a label, 'x of y' or 'a to b'. Setting values are interpolated into the definitions.
The script calls setDTthreads(1), so the stated run time and memory hold on a shared machine.
The profile carries extra columns: zone, DML flags, step 05's meth.diff for tested CpGs, libraries with reads, and min and max relative coverage per class.
left_out: No model refit in the leave-one-out (the verifying agent used glm with p < 2e-4): left out by instruction.
Share of soft-masked bases in the block (the agent's 10%): not computed, because Biostrings drops letter case and it was not a target.
Relative coverage at the three places that hold second copies: the script reports only whether the cutoff is reached there (it is not), because medians would need a second pass over the 22 files.
Coverage beyond 10 kb either side of the region (the agent looked at 100 kb): not in the script.
README.md and issues.md were not edited, by rule; proposed text is in the caveats and in readme_row.
caveats: The cohort difference in the size of the excess cannot be attributed. Cohort, stock and sequencing batch coincide (I-01, I-08), and control libraries are somewhat higher within both classes, so part of it may be a batch effect on the coverage of this GC-richer block.

'Carries the excess' is a threshold on a continuous quantity. Three heat triploids sit just above it (zr3534_6, _7, _8: 1.04 to 1.22 times the cutoff, 29 to 42 of 54 CpGs), and they are what moves the Fisher p for cohort from 0.19 to 0.012.

The issue's sentence that the heat loci are 'not methylation regulated by heat' is supported for the 22-library analysis: without zr3534_4 the median heat difference is -5.66 points and no CpG passes. Among the 9 libraries without the excess, 24 CpGs still exceed 20 points for heat and 37 for ploidy, with groups of 3 and 6. That reflects the four heat-cohort diploids at 34% to 43% and is description only.
Each library is treated as one animal. The sample sheet names the animal for the heat cohort only (I-36).
Run time was measured with the machine under load (load average about 5). Peak memory varied between 1.45 and 1.53 GB across runs.
The 06_diagnostics README needs the row below and the line `Rscript 06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R` in its run list.
An exploration file (explore_window.rds) was written to the repository root by mistake early on and moved to scratch within a minute.

Exploration not in the script, so not reproducible from the repository: within 100 kb either side no CpG outside the block reaches a cutoff, and median coverage at the two larger second-copy places is ordinary in all 22 libraries.

Proposed text for issues.md, I-09, bullet 1: The block of excess coverage is NC_047563.1:39,633,065-39,636,662 (3.6 kb, 82 CpG sites, 56 of them tested, all removed by the filter): the CpGs at which at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff. The 5 kb on either side have ordinary coverage (0.56 to 1.72 times the library median) and no CpG at the cutoff. The ends are those of the cutoff rule; the nearest CpG sites, 182 and 183 bp away, are at 2.5 and 1.3 times the library median in the libraries with the excess.

Proposed text, bullet 2 (replaces 'The excess is not in every animal ... no association with ploidy or cohort'): The excess is in every library and differs in size. All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.3 to 32 times). In 13 the median coverage of the 54 tested CpGs is 10.6 to 35.5 times the library median and reaches the cutoff; in the other 9 it is 2.0 to 5.9 times, with no CpG at the cutoff. The 13 are found in all four groups (4 of 10 heat, 9 of 12 control; 5 of 11 diploid, 8 of 11 triploid). Ploidy shows no difference (Fisher exact p = 0.39; size of the excess, Wilcoxon p = 0.56). Cohort does: the Fisher test on the 13 gives p = 0.19, but with all 54 CpGs required at the cutoff (1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012, and the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). A repeat carried equally by every animal would not give this spread. The pattern is a copy-number difference among individual animals that is larger in the control cohort; cohort, stock and sequencing batch cannot be separated (I-01, I-08).

Proposed text, bullet 3: keep, with 'at most 1 ploidy DML' and add: all 54 CpGs have q < 0.01, so the 20-point rule alone decides; the counts are recomputed differences without a refit; leaving out any other single library leaves 50 to 53 and 29 to 53; zr3534_4 supplies 39% of the heat group's normalized reads. The 9 libraries without the excess alone (6 diploid, 3 triploid; 6 heat, 3 control) still give 37 and 24 CpGs above 20 points.

Proposed text, bullet 4: replace 'Wilcoxon p = 0.007, and p = 0.012 without zr3534_4' by 'exact Wilcoxon p = 0.005, and p = 0.010 without zr3534_4'. The heat cohort (0.008) and control cohort (0.09) values stand.

Proposed text, bullet 5 (replaces 'mostly single-copy'): 69% of the block's 30-mers occur once in the reference (2,471 of 3,570; 42 of 60 in the first sample). 874 occur exactly twice; 474, 294 and 100 of the second copies lie at NC_047560.1:13,874,789-13,881,520, NC_047559.1:4,498,648-4,509,003 and NC_047561.1:36,696,412-36,696,653, where no CpG reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times. The block is not in the transposable element track (nearest records 799 bp before and 585 bp after). It lies inside introns of LOC105317102 and LOC105318567, and 3,471 of its 3,599 bases lie in the lncRNA gene LOC105341636, exons and introns at the same coverage (18.9 and 20.5 times the library median), so the extra copies are genomic. GC content is 42.5% against 30.9% and 32.7% in the flanks.
result.readme_row: | `locus_nc047563.R` | What the locus of I-09 is: the largest run of DML of all three legacy lists, on NC_047563.1, whose tested CpGs the upper coverage filter removes. From the 22 raw coverage files, the step 05 and step 07 tables, the feature tracks and the reference: the block of excess coverage around the region and the coverage of its flanks; which libraries carry the excess and how they are spread over ploidy and cohort (Fisher exact tests under two rules, Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess); how many CpGs still pass the difference threshold when one library at a time is left out (difference rule only, no refit); percent methylation per library by ploidy (exact Wilcoxon tests); genes, exons and transposable elements at the block; GC content, the share of its 30-mers that occur once in the reference, and where the second copies lie. About 2 minutes and 1.5 GB on one core; needs the coverage files and the reference genome in the cache. Issues I-05 and I-09. | `locus_nc047563_summary.csv` (one row per fact, with its definition), `locus_nc047563_per_library.csv`, `locus_nc047563_leave_one_out.csv`, `locus_nc047563_coverage_profile.csv` |

result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in about 4 minutes (3.7 to 4.1 measured, single thread, peak 1.2 to 1.5 GB), and two consecutive runs of the finished script gave byte-identical CSV files (md5 compared). It reads only step 05 and step 07 tables, the seven tracks and the sample sheet; the raw coverage files are not needed.

What it computes, for both modes, both DML lists and seven tracks (264 rows in feature_odds_matched.csv): (1) odds ratios against all tested and against eligible CpGs, checked in the script against step 07 (all 56 cells equal; the script stops otherwise); (2) Mantel-Haenszel within 5-point methylation bins; (3) within bin and decile of within-group SD; (4) ranges 5-95 and 15-85; (5) transposable elements by coverage quartile; (6) CDS against intron within genes; (7) block-bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples of 100 kb windows) for 1 (eligible), 2 and 3; (8) for ploidy, 1,000 label permutations within cohort, plus 1,000 that also keep the acute heat shock balanced.

Legacy results, ploidy then heat. Gene body: 7.08 and 6.14 against all tested; 2.52 and 2.20 against eligible; 2.04 and 1.68 within methylation bins; 1.13 (block interval 0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36) within bin and SD decile. After matching: CDS 1.25 and 1.17, intron 0.81 and 0.87, transposable element 1.05 and 1.02, intergenic 0.80 and 0.92. Shuffled ploidy labels (within cohort): gene-body odds ratio against eligible CpGs median 2.61 (2.5th to 97.5th percentile 1.41 to 4.47), the real 2.52 reached in 54.7% of permutations; median 742.5 CpGs called per permutation (5th to 95th percentile 532 to 1,376), 13.5% reach 1,038. Corrected mode reads the same (gene body 2.85 to 1.24 for ploidy, 2.02 to 0.94 for heat after matching; permutation median 3.11, real value reached in 66.5%).

One addition beyond the task list, because issues.md changed while I worked (commit 68a8a1b, 07:14, added a fifth row to the second table of I-41 from a scratch run): the script also computes the matched comparison 3 for every shuffled-label list, with the within-group SD and its deciles recomputed for the groups the shuffled labels define. Result (legacy, within cohort): gene body median 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), real 1.13 reached in 44%; CDS median 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. With acute heat shock also balanced: 1.08 (0.58 to 2.33) and 1.17 (0.83 to 1.44), 26%. This reproduces the integration check's 1.10 (0.58 to 2.33), 1.18 (0.87 to 1.46) and 29%. The script therefore now writes all five rows of that table.

q-value rule, counted from the diffmeth tables: for ploidy every CpG above 20 points also has q below 0.01 (1,038 of 1,038 legacy, largest q 0.0046; 952 of 952 corrected, largest q 0.0052), and the script stops if that fails. For heat one CpG of 2,352 fails the q rule in legacy mode (q 0.018), none of 2,273 in corrected mode. Heat rows in both permutation tables carry NA and the sentence that no permutation exists.

Two targets depart, both explained under targets: transposable element in the top coverage quartile for ploidy is 0.21, not 0.20 (the script keeps the one ploidy DML outside the eligible range, as step 07 does); the share of eligible CpGs called at a mean of 10% to 20% is 0.37%, not 0.30% (the 300-permutation run under-sampled labellings with very many calls; issues.md already says 0.3% to 0.4%).

Checks done outside the script (scratch, not reproducible from the repository): the Mantel-Haenszel estimates were recomputed with table() and mantelhaen.test on factors (identical); the block intervals with a slow weighted-table implementation (identical at 200 resamples); 40 permutations per scheme and mode were recomputed without pruning and with table() plus fisher.test (counts and all seven odds ratios identical); 25 permutations per scheme for the matched odds ratios (identical in legacy, within 4e-4 in corrected, one CpG at a decile boundary); the pruning of never-callable CpGs was identical to full evaluation on 40 permutations.

Proposed text for I-41 (second table, legacy; replaces scratch numbers by those of the script): shuffled labels against eligible CpGs, 1,000 permutations within cohort: gene body 2.61 (1.41 to 4.47), CDS 1.56, transposable element 0.44; real gene-body value reached in 55%, real CDS value (1.68) in 31%. Same lists, same matching: gene body 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), CDS 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. Matched row: 1.13 (0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36). For I-06: median 742.5 (5th to 95th percentile 532 to 1,376), 13.5% at or above 1,038; with acute heat shock balanced 750 (516 to 1,748), 15.3%. "Status of the pipeline" can now name 06_diagnostics/feature_odds_matched.R as the diagnostic that writes that table.

I ran no git command that changes state; the snapshot commits of the main session picked the files up (the working tree was clean for 06_diagnostics at the end).

A vectorised Mantel-Haenszel formula used for the resamples is checked against mantelhaen.test inside the script. No literature is cited, because I could not check the papers.

Strata: 5-point bins closed on the left over 0 to 100; deciles of within-group SD among eligible CpGs (global, not within bin). Strata without a DML, without another CpG, or without variation in the track add nothing; the output gives strata used and DML in them.
Within-group SD: pooled around the four group means (ploidy by cohort), 18 degrees of freedom, one matrix formula used for the real and the shuffled labels.

Block interval: percentile bootstrap, 2,000 resamples of the 100 kb windows that hold a compared CpG (4,399 legacy, 4,348 corrected), the same resamples for every list, track and comparison of a mode; the Fisher conditional estimate is recomputed on each resample. Bootstrap rather than jackknife because the jackknife interval assumes a normal log odds ratio, which fails where one window holds most DML of a track (53 of 65 ploidy DML in lncRNA).

Permutation as specified (within cohort, 5 and 5, 6 and 6), 1,000 draws, the same labellings for both modes. A second scheme (also balanced on acute heat shock, 3 and 3, 2 and 2) is reported beside it, because the verification used it and the real labels are balanced over it. Results barely differ except in the upper tail of the counts.

The 20-point rule is evaluated on cross-multiplied whole numbers, so a difference of exactly 20 is never called through rounding (in scratch, floating-point arithmetic called 9 of 25 such ties in 40 permutations). With the real labels this rule reproduces the step 05 list exactly; the script checks it.

CpGs whose per-library percentages span no more than the threshold are skipped in the permutation loop. This is exact (a pooled percentage is a weighted mean) and was confirmed against full evaluation in scratch; it brings 1,000 permutations from about 75 to about 15 seconds.

Added: comparison 3 for every shuffled-label list, with SD and deciles recomputed for the shuffled groups, to reproduce the fifth row that entered the I-41 table during this task. With the real labels this code path must return comparison 3; the script checks it.
Added: the number of CpGs called when the ploidy labels are exchanged in one cohort only (3,480 legacy, 3,427 corrected), because it explains the largest permutation counts (3,667 and 4,107).
Mean coverage is the mean of the normalized coverage columns of the united table, quartile cut among eligible CpGs, so the raw coverage files are not read.

Outputs: four CSV files, long format, odds ratios rounded to 4 decimals. The required column names are kept; interval_method, estimate_method and four count columns are added. The within-group SD medians go to a fourth file, feature_odds_matched_within_group_sd.csv, which also shows the balance inside each SD decile.
Randomness: set.seed(20261119) before the label draws, set.seed(20261120) before the block resamples of each mode. data.table threads follow config$cores (default 1).
left_out: Nothing of items (a) to (h) is left out.

Recomputing q-values under shuffled labels: not feasible (a model fit at 480,579 CpGs per permutation). The script applies the difference rule only and says so; a count per permutation is an upper bound on what the full rule would call.

Numbers that entered I-41 during the task and are not in the task list: matching with coverage added (1.23, and 1.48 in a regression), the matched odds ratios without the locus of I-09 (1.02, 0.97, 0.99, 0.89), the share of DML by coverage quartile, and the comparison with binomial sampling (18 against 9.8 points). They still rest on scratch runs.
Block intervals for comparisons 4, 5 and 6, p-values, and the list of loci in both DML lists: not asked for.
A label permutation for heat: none exists; the outputs say so.
caveats: The permutation summaries rest on 1,000 random labellings. Standard errors: about 1 to 1.6 points for the shares, about 10 CpGs for the median count, and the 95th percentile of the count moves by 100 or more between samples. Block-interval ends move by a few percent between seeds.

Quantile strata: a CpG at a decile boundary can change side with floating-point details on another platform or BLAS, which could alter a fourth decimal of a matched odds ratio. On this machine two runs are byte-identical.

Observation from scratch work, not reproduced by the script and worth a follow-up under I-02, I-06 and I-07: the upper tail of the permutation counts is made of labellings close to an exchange of ploidy labels in one cohort. In legacy mode the within-cohort ploidy differences correlate at -0.30 across CpGs, and of the 969 CpGs whose difference exceeds 20 points in both cohorts 788 have opposite signs. Diploid heat is the outlying group (about 13,000 CpGs differ by more than 20 points from diploid control and from triploid heat, against 3,349 between the two control groups). With the heat cohort at its real labels, almost any relabelling of the control cohort calls more CpGs than the real labels (median 1,530 against 1,038). The script only writes the count for the exchanged labelling (3,480).

Matching on deciles is coarse in principle, but in scratch the matched gene-body odds ratio was 1.16, 1.13, 1.12, 1.11 for 5, 10, 20, 40 SD groups (heat 1.03, 1.01, 1.00, 1.00), so the result does not hinge on it.

The matched comparison removes the gene-body excess but shuffled-label lists still show a CDS odds ratio of 1.17 after the same matching, so matching does not make the background fully fair; the permutation columns are the reference to read the real values against.
issues.md, the comment in step 07 and dml_eligible() were edited by other sessions while I worked (text only; no input of the script changed). The targets in the task reflect the earlier text.
The header gives a few expected values as comments (1,038 of 1,038; 952 of 952; one of 2,352; 53 of 65). They are not used by the code and would need editing if step 05 changes.

Repeats the odds ratios of step 07 and stops if they differ; then compares DML with eligible CpGs of the same 5-point methylation bin, of the same bin and decile of within-group SD, with other ranges of mean methylation (5% to 95%, 15% to 85%), by coverage quartile (transposable elements) and CDS against intron; adds intervals from a bootstrap over 100 kb blocks. result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in 2 to 3 minutes at 1.2 GB, and reproduces every target of parts (a) to (f) exactly. Two consecutive runs of the finished script gave byte-identical CSV files.

Part (g) departs from its target because of the unit of the test totals, not because of an error on either side:
- **As step 09 tests** (totals in lines of the universe map, which is what the task asks for): 555 of 12,720 BP terms have p < 0.01 for the accession-run list, against a median of 47 for 200 random lists of the same size (range 8 to 287).
- **With one entry per transcript** (what the verifying agent ran, as issues.md itself says): 1,041, the target, against a median of 47.5 (range 9 to 256). The script's first ten draws are the agent's ten draws and give its 52.5 (13 to 157).
- Nine of the ten legacy top BP terms are below 0.01 in both units; the exception is GO:0035561.
- The legacy list itself gives 383 terms, with p-values equal to those of step 09.

The script also regenerates the size-matched check that issues.md assigns to it, and this changes one statement there. At the size of the legacy list (612 transcripts), position alone does not raise the number of terms under the totals the legacy test used: median 36 for lists drawn from the run against 43.5 for lists from the whole universe. The "about doubles" of issues.md holds only with transcript totals (81 against 38). The reason is that run transcripts have 2.14 map lines each against 1.79 for the universe, and the line totals count that against a list from the run.

A second small correction: ploidy survivors do not come from five linkage groups only. 608 of the 623 lie on the first five, 9 on four of the other five, and 6 on unplaced scaffolds.

What the script stops on: any of the four reads not returning the rows predicted from the quote rule of scan(); its counts differing from `legacy_reader_loss.csv` or `legacy_funnel.csv`; its legacy p-values differing from `legacy_fisher_ploidy_BP.csv`; or the direct hypergeometric computation used for the random lists not matching topGO bit for bit on the two fixed lists. I confirmed four altered-input cases in scratch copies (an apostrophe removed, a nine-field line, a comment character, a missing table); each stopped with a plain message and wrote no file.

No README, helper, pipeline script, run_config.R or issues.md was edited, and I ran no state-changing git command. The parent session's check-in commits picked up the script and outputs while I worked; `git diff HEAD` is empty for all four files.

result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root, and reproduces every target number of I-05 exactly. Three full runs took 5.9 to 6.6 minutes on one core with a peak of 1.6 GB; the four CSV files are byte-identical between the two final runs.

What it does:
- (a) One pass over the 22 coverage files gives the cutoff of each library for bases 1, 2 and 10, and a pooled cutoff of 88 reads.
- (b) Nine filter rules are applied to the 480,579 legacy CpGs. The rule of corrected mode reproduces the positions of `united_cpg_corrected.csv.gz` and the three corrected DML lists; the script stops if it does not.
- (c) The 26,024 removed CpGs are described by number of libraries at the cutoff, repeat track, mitochondrial sequence and runs.
- (d) The q-value rule is counted in the step 05 tables of both modes.

Beyond the letter of (d), I added two checks, because "not binding in two modes" does not by itself prove the counts exact for the other rules:
- **Scaling:** no rule changes the median coverage of any library, so p-values and differences at kept CpGs are those of legacy mode.
- **q-values:** estimated again with methylKit's own SLIM function on the kept CpGs of each rule, they give the legacy lists locus for locus under all nine rules. This costs about 4.5 of the 6 minutes.

Findings not yet in `issues.md`:
- In random sets of 26,024 tested CpGs, the share in runs of 10 or more is 0.53% (median of 1,000 seeded draws; largest 1.00%), against 62.31% observed.
- The share in such runs rises with the number of libraries at the cutoff: 43.1% (one library), 67.3% (2 to 21), 96.6% (all 22).
- The one legacy heat candidate that fails the q-value rule is kept only under "more than half" and "all 22 libraries", and fails there too (re-estimated q 0.0183 and 0.0180).
- Of the removed CpGs, 4,122 are on unplaced scaffolds, out of 24,592 tested there.

Proposed text for I-05 (I did not edit `issues.md`):
- After the table of four definitions: "Four further readings: removal only above the cutoff, 455,253 CpGs (952, 2,273, 159); removal when at least 2 libraries are at their cutoff, 462,296 (957, 2,285, 159); more than half of the libraries, 475,175 (1,002, 2,322, 176); all 22 libraries, 478,611 (1,038, 2,351, 200)."
- Replace "which is exact because the q-value criterion is not binding (last point below)" with: "which is exact: no rule changes the median coverage of a library, so scaling factors, p-values and differences at retained CpGs are those of legacy mode, and q-values estimated again with methylKit's SLIM function on the retained CpGs of each rule give the same lists, locus for locus."
- Add to the removed-CpG point: "In random sets of 26,024 tested CpGs the share in such runs is 0.5% (median of 1,000 draws; largest 1.0%)."
- Add a source line: "Reproducible with `06_diagnostics/coverage_filter_variants.R` (tables `coverage_filter_*.csv`)."

The README run block also needs the line `Rscript 06_diagnostics/coverage_filter_variants.R`.

design_decisions: Cutoffs come from a per-library coverage histogram, with a type-7 quantile function that copies the arithmetic of stats::quantile. The script stops unless each of the 66 cutoffs (22 libraries, 3 bases) is identical to the pipeline helper upper_coverage_cutoff() on the raw values. The pooled cutoff uses the same function on the summed histograms.

Base 10 is read from the installed methylKit (formals of methRead, mincov), base 2 from config$import_min_coverage, and base 1 is a setting. Rule labels and column names are built from these values, so no base number is typed twice.

Files are handled as the helpers do: read_cov(), the cutoff from every line, and the tested CpGs looked up with line 1 lost (first_line_lost("legacy")). The script stops unless the recount with line 1 lost and the recount with every line read both give the legacy CpG set.

Checks against step 05 stop the script with a message: the dml files equal the two rules applied to the diffmeth tables, p-values and differences are identical between modes at common CpGs, and the histograms give the CpG numbers, medians and cutoffs of both library_filtering tables. Eight negative tests with perturbed inputs each stopped with the intended message.

Addition beyond (d), part 1: for each rule, the number of libraries whose median coverage over kept CpGs differs from legacy mode (column libraries_with_changed_median). Zero means the scaling factors, and so the per-CpG p-values and differences, are unchanged. It is 0 for all nine rules.

Addition beyond (d), part 2: q-values are estimated again on the kept CpGs of each rule with methylKit's p.adjusted(method = "SLIM"), the function calculateDiffMeth calls. The script stops unless this reproduces the stored q-values of both modes within a relative 1e-9. If this is judged out of scope it can be removed without touching the rest, apart from one column and 18 rows.
The three rules that count libraries have no methylKit counterpart. They are defined as dropping CpGs from the united legacy table after the libraries were scaled; the header states this.

A run is defined as in the verification and in step 07: removed CpGs on one sequence no more than 1,000 bp apart, with kept CpGs allowed in between. I added a reference from 1,000 random sets of the same size (seed 20261119, Mersenne-Twister, rejection sampling); nothing else in the script is random.
The removed-CpG table has one row per set of CpGs (tested, kept, removed, and removed by 1, 2 to 21, or all 22 libraries), so each share has its comparison in the same table.
Output names follow the explicit list in the task (coverage_filter_cutoffs.csv and so on), not the general pattern <name>*.csv, which only the first file matches.

The repeat share is computed with the pipeline helpers (read_feature_track("TE"), cpg_ranges, overlaps_track). The script reads no step 04 or step 07 table, to keep its dependencies to step 05 and the raw files.
The script calls setDTthreads(config$cores), so it is single-threaded unless WGBS_CORES is raised. No data.table call uses a variable that shares a name with a column; values are assigned with set().
left_out: Nothing in the specification was left out.
Not in the specification and not covered: the sentence of I-05 on step 04's counts at 1x and 20x under base 1 (5,811,796 and 12,890). Only the 10x count of that sentence (451,328) is reproduced here.
caveats: The DML counts of the alternative rules are not refits. They are the legacy DML at kept CpGs, shown to be what step 05 would give by the two checks above. For the three rules that count libraries, the unchanged scaling is true by how the rules are defined, not a finding.

The q-value re-estimation uses an unexported methylKit function (p.adjusted, through getFromNamespace) and starts from p-values stored with 15 significant digits. It was validated against the stored q-values of both modes, but it depends on methylKit internals as of 1.28.0.

The 62.3% depends on the run definition. With a stricter one (consecutive tested CpGs all removed, no kept CpG in between) I obtained 47.4% in a scratch exploration; the script does not compute that number.

The header says "about 7 minutes"; the measured runs were 5.9, 6.3 and 6.6 minutes on a shared machine. I left the comment unchanged so that the file on disk is exactly the one that produced the outputs.
The orchestrator's snapshot commits already track the script; the four CSV files are untracked. I ran no git command that changes state.

My raw coverage matrix and histograms are identical to the verifying agent's independent awk pass (its cand_matrix.rds and hist files). Scratch work, unit tests, negative tests and run logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/build-coverage_filter_variants.
result.readme_row: | `coverage_filter_variants.R` | How far the CpG and DML counts depend on how the upper coverage filter of the Methods is read. From the 22 coverage files: the 99.9th percentile cutoff of each library with the percentile taken over CpGs with at least 1, 2 or 10 reads, and one pooled cutoff; nine filter rules applied to the CpGs of legacy mode, with the CpGs kept and the legacy DML at kept CpGs; what the rule of corrected mode removes (number of libraries at the cutoff, repeat track, mitochondrial sequence, runs of removed CpGs with a reference from 1,000 seeded random draws); and whether those DML counts are what step 05 would report under each rule (q-value rule in the step 05 tables, library medians, q-values estimated again with methylKit's SLIM function). result.verdict:
The script is sound and can be accepted after small changes. No reported number is wrong and no check is vacuous.

- **Runs:** three runs in the repository and one in a clean copy of HEAD (made with `git archive`) all exit 0 without a warning. They take 88 to 108 seconds on one thread with a peak of 1.53 GB. The four CSV files are byte-identical across all runs and with the committed copies.
- **Numbers:** every value of the four tables was reproduced with code that shares nothing with the script (mawk on the raw files, base R without data.table or the helpers, hand-written quantile, Fisher and exact Wilcoxon, mawk on the GFF and BED tracks, Python with numpy on the reference).
- **Checks:** I evaluated the script's own check lines on altered objects. Exchanged library columns, one count off by one, exchanged ploidy labels, another difference threshold and positions shifted by one base each stop the script.
- **Code rules:** library order, strata, coordinates (0-based starts, BED, GFF, 1-based sequence), data.table scoping, paths and the style rules hold. No random numbers are used.

One finding is medium. The header and two summary definitions call the leave-one-out counts the largest possible number of DML. That is false for four libraries (zr3534_1, zr3534_5, zr3534_10, zr3644_17), because 1 to 4 further CpGs of the region become testable without them. The result for zr3534_4 is not affected. The four low findings concern how values are written (a padded "   1", a p-value whose three digits have already been re-rounded to 0.012 in the handoff, a tie created by rounding in the per-library table, two coordinate conventions in one notation).

For issues.md, one sentence of I-09 is not what the script gives: block over flanks is 1.3 to 4.8 and 10.8 to 32.0, not 1.3 to 5.3 and 10.8 to 33.9, which come from another definition. "Mostly single-copy" should carry the full count (69% of the 30-mers once, 874 twice in three places on other linkage groups). "1 ploidy DML" is "at most 1" from the script. The soft-masked shares are not computed by any script.

`R.utils`, needed to read the .gz tables, is not in the `load_packages()` call; this is the known pipeline-wide finding and here it would fail only after the 22 coverage files are read.

I changed nothing in the repository. My code and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review-locus_nc047563/ (mine/recompute_a.R to recompute_g.R, mine/kmers.py, mine/pass.awk, mutation/mutate.R, run1 to run3). The script reviewed is /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R (md5 c11e3c99f8dcd8a3a4f45447a324f9b5).

result.summary:
The script is finished and every target is met: the helper route of step 05 gives exactly what methylKit's own route gives, in both modes. The final script ran twice (549 s and 553 s, peak 1.90 and 1.91 GB, exit status 0) and the three CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs.

State found on resuming: the earlier build agent had written the script and run it once in its last version before the usage limit. I reran that version after the machine restart (outputs byte-identical to the run before the restart), reviewed it against the task and against the methylKit 1.28.0 source, then made one addition and four header corrections.

What the script shows (112 rows; 86 must agree and do, 26 are recorded and not judged):
- Extract of all 22 libraries (2.006% of the CpGs tested in legacy mode, 1.560% in corrected mode): same rows imported and kept, same cutoffs, medians and scaling factors in every library; identical united tables (9,642 and 9,201 CpGs, every count); identical meth.diff, p-values and q-values for both contrasts; same DML at all ten thresholds.
- Six whole libraries: methylKit's methRead and filterByCoverage keep the same rows as read_filtered_counts (22.9 and 22.8 million rows, none differs) and reproduce the records of step 05.
- I-38 and I-05 in methylKit's own objects: the default header loses line 1 and no other row; the misspelled filter arguments are ignored in all 22 libraries.
- Tables of step 05 inside the regions hold the raw counts scaled by scale_counts_like_methylkit (0 of 636,372 and 0 of 467,874 values differ).
- Synthetic counts: 0 of 7,200,240 values differ between normalizeCoverage and scale_counts_like_methylkit, with 792,545 values exactly halfway before rounding.

What I added: both verifying agents had run methylKit's route with the covariate data frames of the legacy script (character vectors), which is why their target says "identical meth.diff" and not "identical p-values". design_decisions: Extract: first 6 Mb of NC_047559.1, 300 kb around NC_047563.1:39,633,323, the mitochondrial sequence, five unplaced scaffolds (one with coverage 6 to 11 times the median, two with many tested CpGs, one on which a file begins, one that 12 libraries lack), and the position of the first line of every file taken from every library. Lines stay in file order and percentages are carried as text, so the files are lines of the originals; written to tempdir() and deleted at the end.

methylKit's route follows the task: legacy mode leaves methRead at header = TRUE with mincov = config$import_min_coverage and filters with lo.count only; corrected mode passes header = FALSE and hi.perc. It is run twice per mode, once per treatment vector, as the legacy script did; the helper route uses reorganize() as step 05 does.

The helper route calls read_filtered_counts, key_to_position, scale_counts_like_methylkit, make_methylraw, unite and reorganize in the order of fit_mode() in step 05. Step 05 does not offer that chain as a function, so the chain is repeated, not reimplemented.

Both routes are tested with the covariates as step 05 passes them, so they differ only in how the counts are built. The legacy coding (character vectors, built from the sample sheet and checked against the vectors typed in the legacy script) is fitted once more on methylKit's route in both modes: legacy mode is then the legacy call end to end, and corrected mode is that call with its two defects fixed.

Three rules, in a column of the table. identical: counts, positions and sets; any difference fails. tolerance: floating-point values; fails above a relative difference of 1e-12, and n_different still counts values that are not bit-identical. recorded: an expected difference, not judged (step 04's order, p and q under the legacy coding, the corrected CpG set of step 05 against the extract). The script stops at the end if any judged row differs, after writing the tables.

Under the legacy coding meth.diff and the DML lists are judged and p-values and q-values are recorded. The DML lists of legacy mode must be those of the legacy call, so a difference there should stop the script.

A whole-library part beyond the task: import and filter of six libraries through methylKit and through the helper, and against the records of step 05. This is the statement of I-05 and of the helper comment, and it covers the real cutoffs (59 to 112 reads), which the extract cannot.
A part beyond the task that ties the tables step 05 wrote to the raw counts inside the regions, so the equivalence is tied to the files the pipeline uses.

Synthetic counts: 20 sets of four libraries of 30,001 CpGs after set.seed(20261119), three draws per CpG and two per set; medians chosen so that the factors are 1, 1.5, 1.25 and one arbitrary ratio, which forces exact ties.

Step 04's order is checked on rows selected by step 04's own rule, at 1 read and at config$min_coverage reads, with the effect on percent methylation and on the correlations; at config$min_coverage the selection must reproduce the united CpGs and factors of the helper route or the script stops.
Three small CSV files (25 KB, 10 KB, 2 KB); nothing per CpG. The main table carries the methylKit version.
left_out: methylKit's own route on the 22 whole libraries at once: not run, because it needs about 9 GB against a limit of 3 GB. In its place: both routes on the extract, import and filter on six whole libraries, the counts of step 05 against raw counts, and the synthetic ties.
Whole-library comparison for the other 16 libraries: left out for run time (about 13 s per library and mode; all 22 in both modes would add about 7 minutes).

The tie of the tables of step 05 to the raw counts outside the regions of the extract (a second agent's 31.7 and 30.0 million values): not done; only the lines of the regions are kept. It could be added to the extraction pass for about half a minute if wanted.
Nothing of task items (a) to (e) or of the step 04 check is left out. Legacy mode has no upper cutoff to compare, because no upper filter runs there.
caveats: On the extract the corrected-mode cutoffs are 182 to 701 reads, against 59 to 112 on the whole files, because the extract is rich in deeply covered sequence. The same rule runs at other values: the upper filter removes 2,628 rows there, and 200 of the 363 mitochondrial CpGs stay in the united table. Cutoffs of the whole files are exercised only in the six whole libraries.

No first-line CpG has 10 reads in all 22 libraries, so the first-line rule changes rows per library (8 libraries at import, 1 among the kept rows) and never the united table. That is a property of the data.

The sentence in 06_diagnostics/README.md that no comparison on the complete 22 libraries in corrected mode is on record stays true in the strict sense: for whole libraries the script compares import and filter of six. Which CpGs each mode keeps on the whole files is checked by the sibling script coverage_filter_variants.R.
The helper chain is copied from fit_mode(). If step 05 changes its chain this script must follow; a stale table of step 05 would be caught only inside the regions.

The header sentence on the glm.fit warnings rests on a scratch test, not on the script: 1,433 of the 1,435 CpGs with a warning in legacy mode have methylated reads only in libraries of one ploidy and one cohort. The header says it was looked at once.
The header statements on what methylKit does were checked against the installed 1.28.0 source only.

The script is long (933 lines) and does more than the task lists: whole libraries, the two legacy defects, the legacy coding, the tie to the tables of step 05. A reviewer should read those parts as additions.
Run time depends on the machine: the earlier version took 7.3 minutes when quiet and 10.8 minutes under load; the final version took 9.0 minutes twice with two other R processes running.
My scratch directory still holds two copies of the extract (232 MB) and the awk recount; nothing there is needed by the script.
result.readme_row: | `check_methylkit_equivalence.R` | Shows that the low-memory import of step 05 (`02_R_functions/methylkit_helpers.R`) gives what methylKit's own `methRead`, `filterByCoverage`, `normalizeCoverage` and `unite` give, in both modes (issues I-05, I-38). Both routes run on a regional extract of all 22 coverage files that keeps the first line of every file (2.0% of the CpGs tested in legacy mode, 1.6% in corrected mode): the same rows kept, cutoffs, medians and scaling factors in every library, identical united tables (9,642 and 9,201 CpGs), and identical differences, p-values, q-values and DML lists for both contrasts. Also compared: import and filter on six whole libraries, with methylKit and with the records of step 05; the counts of step 05 inside the regions with the raw counts; rounding on synthetic counts with exact ties. Recorded, not judged: p-values under the covariate coding of the legacy script (within 2e-8, relative; same DML lists), and the order of operations of step 04 (at most 25 of 3.3 million scaled counts of the extract differ; correlations change by less than 1e-5). Stops if a comparison that must agree does not. About 9 minutes, 2 GB, one core; needs the coverage files and the tables of step 05. Written by an agent; review pending | `check_methylkit_equivalence.csv` (one row per comparison), `check_methylkit_equivalence_libraries.csv` (one row per library, mode and scope), `check_methylkit_equivalence_extract.csv` (one row per region of the extract) |

findings.summary: The tail statistics of the label permutation (95th percentile of CpGs called, share of permutations reaching the real number, share of eligible CpGs called by methylation bin, 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) carry a large Monte Carlo error at 1,000 draws, and nothing in the output says so. The two schemes differ on these cells by sampling error only, yet the tables read as a scheme effect.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of feature_odds_label_permutation_counts.csv concludes that balancing the acute heat shock raises the 95th percentile of the count from 1,376 to 1,748, the share reaching 1,038 from 13.5% to 15.3%, and the share called at a mean of 10% to 20% from 0.37% to 0.46%. None of this is real. issues.md then has three values for one quantity (95th percentile 1,235 from dml_sensitivity.R, 1,376 and 1,748 from this script), and the 0.455% contradicts its "0.3% to 0.4%".
findings.evidence: Script, legacy, within cohort and with acute heat shock balanced: 95th percentile 1,376.3 and 1,748.1; share reaching 1,038: 0.135 and 0.153; called at mean 10-20%: 0.374% and 0.455%; gene-body 97.5th percentile 4.47 and 4.26. My complete enumeration of all 232,848 labellings (110,880 balanced on the heat shock): 95th percentile 1,386.8 and 1,461.0; share 0.1283 (29,878 labellings) and 0.1379 (15,288); 10-20% bin 0.386% and 0.403%; median 752 and 749; 5th percentile 520 and 521; gene-body odds ratio median 2.65 (1.46 to 4.52) and 2.65 (1.47 to 4.46), real value reached in 56.2% and 56.4%. Corrected mode: script 1,304 and 1,683, 0.147 and 0.175; exact 1,327 and 1,395, 0.149 and 0.158. The 95th percentile of 1,000 random labellings has a central 95% range of 1,238 to 1,675 (within cohort) and 1,281 to 1,853 (balanced); a value of 1,748 or more occurs in 4.6% of such samples. The enumeration reproduces numbers that I-06 reports from another computation (903 of 924, median 1,530; 40 of 252, median 753.5). Scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review2-feature_odds_matched/work/check_G_enumeration.R, out/G_legacy.log, out/G_corrected.log, out/E_legacy.log.
findings.suggested_fix: For the count summaries (median, percentiles, share reaching the real number, share called by bin and by track) replace the draws by the complete enumeration: pooled counts of the 126 heat-cohort subsets (one of each mirror pair) and the 924 control-cohort subsets on the candidate CpGs, added pairwise; the balanced scheme is a subset. In plain R this took 8 to 9 minutes and 2.3 GB per mode. If that is too long, keep the draws and write beside every percentile its order-statistic 95% interval (here 1,266 to 1,666 and 1,448 to 2,113 for the two 95th percentiles) and beside every share its standard error, and say in the notes column that the schemes differ by sampling error only. The 1,000 draws can stay for the matched odds ratios, with the same intervals.

findings.summary: The ends of the block-bootstrap intervals carry 2% to 4% resampling error at 2,000 resamples and are written to 4 decimals. The header says so; the CSV rows do not.
findings.failure_scenario: The matched gene-body interval for ploidy is quoted as 0.77 to 1.82 from this script, 0.76 to 1.70 in issues.md, and would be 0.75 to 1.76 with another seed; a reader takes the second decimal as determined.
findings.evidence: Same seed and call sequence, own code (resampling by row index, own estimators): 26 of 26 intervals equal in legacy mode, so the script computes what it says. Other seed, 2,000 resamples: 0.7486 to 1.7559 against the script's 0.7725 to 1.8228. 20,000 resamples: 0.7476 to 1.7806; ten batches of 2,000 gave lower ends 0.733 to 0.765 and upper ends 1.729 to 1.816, so the script's seed lies outside the range of ten others at both ends. Heat: 0.7658 to 1.3578 against 0.7646 to 1.3644. Scratch: work/out/H_legacy.log, work/out/B_legacy.log.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise n_boot to 10,000 (the Mantel-Haenszel rows are matrix products; the fisher.test rows would add about 2.5 minutes per mode), or write block intervals to 2 decimals and put the resampling error in the notes column.

findings.summary: In corrected mode four of the nine SD decile cuts coincide with the SD of one eligible CpG, and which decile that CpG gets depends on the last bit of a floating-point number. The script treats them inconsistently: three go to the upper decile, one to the lower.
findings.failure_scenario: On another R build or BLAS, or after an equivalent rewrite of the SD formula, the fourth decimal of some matched odds ratios and two rows of the SD table change; byte-identical output holds per machine only. The script's own check of its two code paths allows 1e-3, so it would not notice.
findings.evidence: 61,056 eligible CpGs give quantile indices 1 + (n - 1)p = 12212, 24423, 36634, 48845 for p = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8. seq(0, 1, length.out = 11)[7] is 0.6000000000000001, so the third index is 36634.000000000007 and that cut is interpolated a hair above the CpG; the other three equal the CpG exactly. With p = 6/10 and the SD from residuals, one CpG changes decile: n_other_eligible of deciles 6 and 7 becomes 6,052 and 6,046 (script 6,053 and 6,045), the matched heat lncRNA odds ratio 0.8505 (script 0.8506), and two matched shares 0.618 and 0.504 (script 0.617 and 0.503). Legacy mode (65,480 eligible) has no whole index and no difference. On this machine (reference BLAS, one thread) the script's two code paths give bit-identical SDs, so the 1e-3 tolerance at line 546 is not needed here. Scratch: work/out/D_corrected.log, work/check_K_sd_table.R.
findings.suggested_fix: Assign SD groups by rank with ties broken by row order, for example ceiling(n_sd_groups * rank(sd, ties.method = "first") / n) among eligible CpGs, in both code paths; then tighten the tolerance at line 546 to 1e-9.

findings.summary: The identity check between methylKit's floating-point rule and the script's exact rule stops the run if a CpG lies at exactly the threshold and its stored difference rounds above it. Such ties exist in the real data.
findings.failure_scenario: After any rerun of step 05 that changes the set of tested CpGs (another coverage filter, another minimum coverage), a tie whose meth.diff is stored as 20.000000000000004 makes stopifnot(identical(...)) fail although nothing is wrong, and the whole script stops.
findings.evidence: The heat contrast has one CpG at exactly -20 points in both modes (NW_022994958.1:20934, q 0.00039 and 0.00045); it happens to be stored as -20, so the check passes. Under shuffled labels a floating-point evaluation of the same rule misjudged 125 of 578 exact ties (within cohort) and 101 of 596 (balanced), in 120 and 99 of 1,000 permutations. This confirms that the exact rule is needed in the permutation, and shows the size of the risk for the check. Scratch: work/out/C_legacy.log.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the two rules only where abs(abs(meth.diff) - threshold) exceeds 1e-9, write the number of exact ties per contrast to the counts table, and say in the header how step 05 treated them.

findings.summary: count_tab[, value := signif(value, 6)] rounds every value of the counts table to six significant digits, counts included.
findings.failure_scenario: With a united table of 1,000,000 CpGs or more, "tested CpGs" and other counts are written rounded (signif(1234567, 6) is 1,234,570) with no warning.
findings.evidence: Largest value now is 480,579, so the present output is not affected. Line 659 applies signif to the whole column.
findings.suggested_fix: Round only values that are not whole numbers.

findings.summary: Odds ratios and Fisher limits are written to 4 decimals, but fisher.test finds its estimate and limits with a root tolerance of about 1e-4 relative, so the last digits are not determined.
findings.failure_scenario: A comparison with other software, or with a higher-precision recomputation, differs in the fourth significant digit and is taken for an error. Step 07 holds the same values, so the script's equality check passes.
findings.evidence: Heat, gene body, all tested CpGs (2,203/148/338,503/139,725): fisher.test gives 6.144345 (5.199368 to 7.308605). At 7.308605 the tail probability is 0.02491, not 0.025; solving to 1e-13 gives 6.144172 (5.199569 to 7.307619). Ploidy: upper limit 9.4219 against 9.4226; corrected mode 12.4117 against 12.4140. Scratch: work/check_I_fisher_precision.R.
findings.suggested_fix: No change of method (equality with step 07 is the purpose). Write 3 significant digits, or say in the header that fisher.test's values are accurate to about 4 significant digits.

findings.summary: Comparison 4 keeps DML whose mean lies outside the range in the DML row. For 15% to 85% that is 39 ploidy and 73 heat DML compared with a background that holds no CpG at their methylation level. The notes column gives the count; the comparison label does not.
findings.failure_scenario: The row "CpGs with mean methylation 15% to 85%" is read as a comparison inside that range. Restricted to it, the gene-body odds ratios are 2.23 and 1.89, not 2.10 and 1.84.
findings.evidence: Script: 2.1050 and 1.8406 (39 and 73 DML outside). DML inside the range only: 2.2274 and 1.8884; CDS 1.6926 and 1.5890 against 1.7079 and 1.6081; intron 0.7486 and 0.8097 against 0.7357 and 0.8001. The range 5% to 95% has no DML outside, the range 10% to 90% one. Scratch: work/out/F_legacy.log.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the rows with the DML restricted to the range, or name the convention in the comparison label.

result.verdict:
Accept the script. It computes what the task asked, and every number I recomputed with independent code agrees with it; the one change needed before its permutation counts are quoted is a Monte Carlo interval or a complete enumeration.

- **Runs:** two runs from the repository root finished with exit 0 in 238 s each, 1.30 GB peak, one thread, empty stderr. The four CSV files were byte-identical between the runs and to the copies taken beforehand; the script and repository were left unchanged.
- **Reading:** I found no error in strata, group assignment, library order, coordinates, seeds, data.table scoping or paths. The header is accurate, there is no em dash and no "desiccation", and every file read is tracked in git.
- **Recomputation:** base R with my own track reader, overlap rule, conditional odds ratio, Mantel-Haenszel estimate and SD by residuals reproduced all 180 non-bootstrap odds rows, 50 of the 52 block intervals I recomputed (the other two differ by 0.0001), and 361 of 364 permutation cells. All permutation counts are identical. The differences trace to fisher.test's root tolerance and to one CpG on a decile cut.
- **Checks can fail:** three mutated scratch copies (shifted eligible range, CpG shifted by one base, two libraries exchanged) all stopped at the intended check.
- **The medium finding:** the 95th percentile of the count, the share reaching the real number and the share called by bin are unstable at 1,000 draws. The scheme with acute heat shock balanced drew a heavy tail (95th percentile 1,748 against an exact 1,461). The within-cohort scheme the task specified is close to exact (1,376 against 1,387; 13.5% against 12.8%).
- **Low findings:** six, none of which changes a reading.
- **issues.md:** fifteen sentences of I-41 and I-06 need the script's values. No conclusion of I-41 changes: the gene-body excess is gone after matching (1.13 and 1.01) and is reached by shuffled labels in more than half of the labellings. Confirmed without change: the first table, both range sentences, CDS against intron, transposable elements by coverage in both modes, the SD medians and the corrected-mode sentence.
- **Corrected mode adds:** matched gene body 1.24 (block interval 0.85 to 1.96) and 0.94 (0.73 to 1.27). The matched intergenic odds ratio for ploidy stays below 1 (0.59, 0.28 to 0.96), but shuffled labels give the same median (0.59).

The builder's two additions (matched odds under shuffled labels, the second permutation scheme) are correct. Reviewer scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review2-feature_odds_matched/work (logs in out/; the two 300 MB intermediate files were deleted and recompute_A.R rebuilds them in 30 s).

findings.summary: Part (g) does not isolate position. The accession-run list keeps the isoforms of each gene together (11,284 transcripts of 5,264 genes) and is compared with random lists of single transcripts. Random sets of whole genes with no position give as many terms as the run with transcript totals, and more with line totals. The numbers in the CSV are right; the reading in the header is not.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader takes the rows accession_run (555 terms with line totals, 1,041 with transcript totals) against random_universe_size_of_run (median 47 and 47.5) as the effect of position. The header says so (lines 35 to 41: 'To see what position alone does to the test'; line 113: 'so they show what position does'), and so do issues.md I-40 ('A list confined to that run gives more terms below p = 0.01 than a random list of the same size, whatever the DML are'; 'The position skew is therefore a bias of the legacy test') and the builder's proposed replacement text. The difference is the isoform unit of I-03, which the same paragraph names as the alternative explanation.
findings.evidence: Reviewer's own code (GO.db 3.13.0 ancestors, no topGO; it reproduces every number of the position-control CSV and agrees with step 09 p-values to 4.5e-15). 200 random gene sets matched to the run (5,264 whole genes with the run's numbers of transcripts per gene, 11,284 to 11,286 transcripts, seed 15): terms with p < 0.01, transcript totals median 1,072.5 (range 627 to 1,570; 5th to 95th percentile 773 to 1,445) against 1,041 for the run, so 56% of the sets reach the run's count; line totals median 963 (517 to 1,580; 689 to 1,316) against 555 for the run, so 99.5% of the sets reach it. 200 unmatched whole-gene sets (seed 14): medians 1,012 and 1,022.5. topGO itself, called as step 09 calls it, on two matched sets: 761 and 648 (line totals), 814 and 765 (transcript totals). Seven other accession windows of the same size taken whole: 850 to 2,556 (line totals), 1,052 to 1,332 (transcript totals). 'Nine of the ten legacy top terms' is close to a restatement of where the list lies: six of the ten are carried by the 12 or 13 isoforms of one gene inside the run, and their run p-values (8.5e-06 and 2.1e-05 with transcript totals) are the chance that 13 or 12 transcripts all fall in a list of 9,277 of 22,761. In unmatched whole-gene sets the median is 4 of 10 and 4 of 200 sets reach nine. findings.suggested_fix: Add a fourth kind of list: random sets of whole genes with the run's number of genes and of transcripts per gene (200 sets cost seconds with direct_test), and report where the run falls among them. Reword header part (g), the Notes at lines 102 to 114, the section title at line 641 and the two log lines (646, 810): call it an accession-run control and state that the comparison with single-transcript lists shows the isoform unit, not position. Add a column that says whether a kind of list keeps isoforms together. Do not carry 'position' into issues.md or the README row.

findings.summary: At the size of the legacy list, the lists read as 'position' are confined to the accession run, not to the five linkage groups. Lists drawn by linkage group alone show almost no excess, and most of the excess of run lists appears for any pool of whole genes of the run's size.
findings.failure_scenario: random_run_size_of_legacy_list (median 81 with transcript totals, 36 with line totals) against random_universe_size_of_legacy_list (38 and 43.5) is read as 'position alone about doubles the number' (issues.md I-40) or as 'position alone does not raise the number under the legacy totals' (builder's proposed text). Neither is a statement about position. With transcript totals the doubling belongs to confinement to 41% of the universe; with line totals the result is set by how many map lines per transcript the pool has.
findings.evidence: Reviewer's own code, medians of BP terms with p < 0.01 for lists of 612. From all 17,070 universe transcripts of NC_047559.1 to NC_047563.1: 43 to 44 with transcript totals against 38 to 40 for the universe, and 32.5 to 34 against 40 to 41 with line totals (500 draws seed 12; 1,000 draws seed 11); the run in the same runs: 78.5 to 79 and 38. From 12 random pools of whole genes with as many transcripts as the run (150 lists each, seed 13): 53 to 82, median 62 (transcript totals); 43.5 to 86, median 66 (line totals). From 12 other accession windows of the run's size: 66 to 92.5 (transcript totals) and 33 to 238.5 (line totals); the run window 73.5 and 32.5. Map lines per transcript with a BP term: 2.14 in the run, the highest of all windows (1.48 to 2.14), 1.79 in the universe. The run holds 11,241 of the 17,070 universe transcripts of the five linkage groups, all of the XM_034 series; the 5,455 XM_011-series transcripts there are outside it. The script's own medians are stable: 2,000 draws under two other seeds give 36.5 and 38 against 41 and 42 (line totals), 76 and 77 against 38 and 39 (transcript totals). Scripts: position_vs_accession.R, position_vs_accession2.R, window_shift.R, recompute_g.R in the same scratch folder.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the kind as 'confined to the accession run'. To say anything about position, add pools to draw from: the universe transcripts of the linkage groups of the run, and a random pool of whole genes of the run's size. In the Notes say that under line totals the count for a pool depends on its map lines per transcript, which is why the run comes out low.

findings.summary: The comparison of p-values with step 09 uses all.equal(tolerance = 1e-9), which is a mean relative difference over all 12,720 terms, not a per-term tolerance. It cannot detect a wrong small p-value.
findings.failure_scenario: The header (lines 78 to 80) and the builder's report say the p-values equal those of legacy_fisher_ploidy_BP.csv 'within 1e-9'. With the sum of the p-values at 11,675, the check accepts a summed absolute error of about 1.2e-05, so any error in the terms that matter (p from 1e-19 to 1e-3) passes this condition. The two other conditions of the same stopifnot (top-ten set, count below the cutoff) protect what the outputs use, so no reported number is at risk.
findings.evidence: Under the script's conditions (recomputed values differ from the 15-digit CSV values in the last bits): the top term set to 1e-06 in place of 1.0e-19 gives all.equal TRUE; all ten top terms multiplied by 1e6 gives TRUE. The true agreement is far better: largest per-term relative difference 4.5e-15 (reviewer's recomputation without topGO).
findings.suggested_fix: Compare per term: max(abs(p_legacy[go_id] - p_fisher) / p_fisher) < 1e-9.

findings.summary: Two definitions are looser than the data. lines_in_file (and header lines 6 to 7): 'one line per DML, transcript and GO term'; the tables have one line per DML, transcript, GO term and GOslim bin. transcripts_admitted_by_both (line 337): 'the transcripts of interest of the legacy test'; 498 of the 612 take part in the BP test.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the CSV divides lines by transcripts and reads the result as GO terms per transcript and DML, or quotes 612 as the number of transcripts in the BP test.
findings.evidence: Distinct (transcript, DML, GO ID) against lines: ploidy 41,634 against 46,626; heat 93,796 against 106,621; shared 6,440 against 7,029; with the GOslim bin added every line is distinct. Row legacy_list of the position-control CSV: transcripts_in_list 612, transcripts_with_bp_term_median 498; issues.md I-40 calls the 612 an upper bound.
findings.suggested_fix: 'one line per DML, transcript, GO term and GOslim bin'; 'handed to the legacy test as transcripts of interest (those with a term of the ontology take part in each test)'.

findings.summary: The two halves of the linkage groups are typed in as config$linkage_groups[1:5] and [6:10]. The reason is reported (mrnas_in_run_range_by_sequence) but no check ties the split to it, and the same halves are reported for heat and shared, where the run range does not follow them.
findings.failure_scenario: If the ploidy table or the annotation changed so that the run covered other linkage groups, the quantities named first_five and last_five would still be written with their definitions, without a stop.
findings.evidence: Lines 271 to 272; no stopifnot uses mrnas_in_range. For heat the mRNAs of the run range lie on NC_047559.1 to NC_047564.1, NC_047568.1 and unplaced scaffolds (CSV row heat, mrnas_in_run_range_by_sequence).
findings.suggested_fix: After the ploidy table is processed, stop unless the sequences that hold mRNAs of the ploidy run range are the first five linkage groups and unplaced scaffolds; or derive the two groups from that quantity.

result.verdict:
The script is sound as a source of numbers. It runs clean from the repository root (134 s and 131 s, peak memory 1.19 GB), two runs gave byte-identical CSV files that also equal the committed copies, and every number I recomputed with independent code agrees: all of parts (a) to (f), all 612 cells of the linkage-group table, and every row of the position-control table from the same seed. Its checks are real; none is written so that it cannot fail. I found no wrong number, no data.table scoping error, no path or seed problem, and no breach of the memory or style rules.

The problem is what part (g) is read to show. The control it implements, as the task specified it, does not isolate position:
- **Whole run against random lists:** the run list holds whole genes (11,284 transcripts of 5,264 genes) and is compared with lists of single transcripts. Random sets of whole genes with the same isoform numbers and no position give a median of 1,072.5 terms with transcript totals (run 1,041) and 963 with line totals (run 555). The excess over 47 is the isoform unit of I-03 again.
- **Lists of the legacy size:** the excess of run lists with transcript totals (81 against 38) is mostly confinement to any 41% of the universe's genes (random whole-gene pools give a median of 62, other accession windows 66 to 92.5). Lists drawn from the five linkage groups alone give 43 to 44 against 38 to 40.
- **Line totals:** the run comes out low (36 against 43.5) because its transcripts have the most map lines each (2.14 against 1.79).

These comparison figures come from my scratch code, not from the script.

Two of the builder's corrections to issues.md are confirmed: the survivors are not from five linkage groups only, and "about doubles" holds only with one entry per transcript. Neither the current I-40 text nor the builder's proposed replacement should attribute the part (g) differences to position.

Recommended before issues.md is rewritten from this script: add a whole-gene comparison list to part (g) and reword its header, or keep the numbers and drop the word position. The three low findings are a tolerance check that is a mean over all terms, two loose definitions, and the typed-in split of the linkage groups.

I did not modify the script or its outputs. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review-legacy_reader_mechanism/mine; copies of the outputs before and after each run are in the orig, run1 and run2 folders beside it. result.verdict:
Accept. No reported number is wrong, and one medium finding should be fixed before the authors decide on I-05.

- **Runs:** two runs from the repository root exited with status 0 and no warning, in 348 s and 347 s with a peak of 1,602 MB on one core. The four CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs and to the copies I made beforehand. The script and its outputs in the repository are unchanged.
- **Recomputation:** every number in the four CSV files was recomputed with code that shares nothing with the script and agrees. This covers all 66 cutoffs, the pooled cutoff of 88, the nine rules, the corrected-mode positions and DML lists, the removed-CpG table, the q-value table and the unchanged medians.
- **Checks:** four negative tests on a copy in a scratch root each stopped with the intended message: a DML row missing, a CpG missing from the corrected tables, a changed cutoff record, and one stored q-value changed by a relative 1e-6. The functions taken from the script by parsing agree with direct computation on synthetic inputs. The header's account of filterByCoverage and normalizeCoverage matches the installed methylKit 1.28.0 source, and its SLIM code uses no random numbers.
- **Rules of the task:** I found no typed-in result, no absolute path, no dependence on thread count or an unset seed, no data.table scoping hazard, no coordinate error and no non-ASCII character.

Findings:
- **Medium:** the script stops with a bare stopifnot when `import_min_coverage` is 1 or 10, the two other readings that I-05 offers.
- **Low:** the check on line 374 cannot fail, though nothing rests on it.
- **Low:** `libraries_with_changed_median` is 0 by construction for the rules that count libraries, and the table gives no margin.

result.readme_row: | `locus_nc047563.R` | What the locus of I-09 is: the largest run of DML of all three legacy lists, on NC_047563.1, whose tested CpGs the upper coverage filter removes. From the 22 raw coverage files, the step 05 and step 07 tables, the feature tracks and the reference: the block of excess coverage around the region and the coverage of its flanks; which libraries carry the excess and how they are spread over ploidy and cohort (Fisher exact tests under two rules, Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess); how many CpGs still pass the difference threshold when one library at a time is left out, among the CpGs tested with all libraries and among those testable without that library (difference rule only, no refit); percent methylation per library by ploidy (exact Wilcoxon tests); genes, exons and transposable elements at the block; GC content, the share of its 30-mers that occur once in the reference, and where the second copies lie. About 2 minutes and 1.5 GB on one core; needs the coverage files and the reference genome in the cache. Issues I-05 and I-09. | `locus_nc047563_summary.csv` (one row per fact, with its definition), `locus_nc047563_per_library.csv`, `locus_nc047563_leave_one_out.csv`, `locus_nc047563_coverage_profile.csv` |
result.notes:
All five findings of the review are right and are applied; the script runs clean and every target is re-checked. Two things are left for the session: one sentence of `07_documentation/session_handoff.md` and the README row.

**Final state**
- Script: `/home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R`, 831 lines, md5 83577c3f4458637bd19aea5cec79cf98.
- Two runs of that version from the repository root: exit 0, nothing on stderr, 83 and 84 seconds on one thread, peak resident memory 1.45 GB (1.44 to 1.53 GB over the five runs of this stage).
- The four CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs, and the logs are identical apart from time stamps.
- `locus_nc047563_coverage_profile.csv` is unchanged from the reviewed version. The summary has 190 rows (11 new), the leave-one-out table 3 new columns, and the per-library table three decimals in `region_pct_methylation`.
- The script writes exactly these four files, so there was nothing to remove.

**What changed in the numbers**
- Leave-one-out: without zr3534_4 both counts give 1 (ploidy) and 0 (heat) of 54 CpGs, so the headline of I-09 stands. For the other libraries the count over testable CpGs is 50 to 57 (ploidy) and 29 to 53 (heat); over the 54 CpGs it stays 50 to 53 and 29 to 53.
- The Fisher p of the stricter rule by cohort is written 0.011499 instead of 0.0115.

**One departure from the review's wording**
The review asked for four significant digits in p-values. That alone would not have fixed its own example: 0.0114993 is 0.01150 at four digits and would still be written 0.0115. The script now writes four significant digits and adds digits while the last one written is a 5.

**How I checked**
- Separate recomputation (mawk on the 22 coverage files, base R without the helpers) of the region, block, flanks, libraries with the excess, both Fisher tests (hypergeometric sums), all exact Wilcoxon tests (dynamic programme), the normal approximations, every computed column of the leave-one-out table and the profile medians: all equal to the tables.
- The exact tests of part d can now be repeated from the per-library table without a warning about ties.
- Genes, exons and transposable elements with mawk on the tracks; GC content, CG count and the 60 sampled 30-mers with Python on the reference: all equal.
- Four altered copies of the script (outputs redirected to scratch) are each stopped by the new checks: one decimal for percent methylation, a strict coverage rule, the smallest median as scaling base, and coverage in place of numCs + numTs.

**Left for the session**
- `07_documentation/session_handoff.md`, line 71: "Fisher p = 0.012" should read 0.011. I did not edit that file.
- `06_diagnostics/README.md`: the row is in `readme_row`. The run-list line should lose "review pending": `Rscript 06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R   # about 2 minutes; needs the coverage files and the genome`.
- `issues.md`: 15 proposed changes. One is a correction (block over flanks is 1.3 to 4.8 and 10.8 to 32.0, not 1.3 to 5.3 and 10.8 to 33.9); the rest are citations and refinements.
- Two numbers of I-09 have no script behind them: the soft-masked shares (10%, 35% to 37%; my count agrees) and the refit without zr3534_4 (p = 6e-24).
- `R.utils` is still not in the `load_packages()` call (pipeline-wide point, not a finding of this review).
