findings.summary: When the two routes disagree on the rows kept, the script stops inside part 7 (must at lines 826 to 827; a second must of the same kind is at lines 692 to 693) before any table is written, and the message names step 04, not the disagreement between methylKit and the helpers.
findings.failure_scenario: read_filtered_counts or upper_coverage_cutoff is changed (or methylKit changes its filter) so that the helper keeps other rows than methylKit in corrected mode. On the rerun the script exits with 'The rule of step 04 at 10 reads does not give the CpGs and the scaling factors of the helper route in mode corrected.' None of the three CSV files is written, so the rows that had already recorded the real disagreement (rows kept, united CpGs) are lost, and the tables of the last passing run stay in 06_diagnostics and still say 'identical'.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy of the project with one change in the helper, d[coverage <= cutoff] in read_filtered_counts (proj_mutB, mutB.log in my scratch directory): the log shows the helper route testing 9,207 CpGs against 9,201 by methylKit, then the error quoted above, exit status 1, and no CSV in the 06_diagnostics of that copy. Header lines 44 to 45 say that one row is written per comparison and that the script stops if a judged comparison differs; the builder's report says it stops 'after writing the tables'. A change that leaves the kept rows alone ends as designed: with the order of step 04 put into scale_counts_like_methylkit and the first line kept in legacy mode (proj_mutA) the tables are written, 38 rows read DIFFERENT (rows imported in 8 libraries, normalized counts, 16 and 15 united counts, meth.diff, p, q, 12 and 3 counts of the step 05 tables, 3,459 synthetic values) and the error comes at the end. So the judged comparisons can fail; only this failure path is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the two must() calls into judged rows (rule 'identical'), or skip part 7 for a mode whose helper route already differs and record that it was skipped, so that part 8 always writes the tables and the final stop lists the failing rows. Writing the three tables before part 7 would also do.

findings.summary: Every run ends its log with 'There were 45 warnings (use warnings() to see them)'. The header explains the glm.fit warnings only, so a reader cannot tell that these 45 are harmless.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the log sees 45 unexplained R warnings in a script whose purpose is to certify exact agreement, and has to rerun it to find out what they are.
findings.evidence: Run of a scratch copy with options(warn = 1) (baseline.log): 45 times 'Warning in max(i) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf'. methylKit raises it when getMethylDiff selects no row, which happens at the thresholds without DML (40 to 50 points for the legacy ploidy contrast, 35 to 50 for the other three): two per empty threshold from lines 634 and 636 (getMethylDiff on methylKit's fit, dml_table on the helper's fit) and one from line 667; 21 in legacy mode and 24 in corrected mode. Reproduced on a five-row methylDiff object: 0 rows returned and the same warning. The results are right; the selections are empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch this message around the three calls and log its count as is done for the glm.fit warnings, or do not call getMethylDiff when no CpG passes the rule; add one line to Notes.

findings.summary: methylKit's route takes its header argument from first_line_lost(), a helper of the route under test (lines 427 and 480), so the legacy rows of the comparison cannot detect a wrong first-line rule; only the two I-38 rows can, and they are written only when both modes are in config$modes (lines 462 and 702).
findings.failure_scenario: first_line_lost('legacy') is changed to FALSE, or returns the wrong value after an edit. Both routes then read every line in legacy mode and agree with each other. With config$modes = 'legacy' alone the script would pass.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy with first_line_lost() returning FALSE for both modes (proj_mutC): every per-library, united-table, test and DML row of legacy mode still reads 'identical' (1,187,099 rows kept by both routes, where the true legacy import keeps 1,187,098). Only 'rows that methRead returns with header = FALSE and not with its default header = TRUE' (8 of 22 libraries) and its full-library counterpart (2 of 6) differ, and they stop the script. The filter of methylKit's route is chosen from mode_name directly (lines 430 to 431 and 482 to 483); the header is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the legacy call out: if (mode_name == "corrected") read_args$header <- FALSE, in both places, so that methylKit's route does not depend on any helper.

findings.summary: Three labels say more, or something else, than the statistic. (a) The row 'upper cutoff: the percentile that filterByCoverage computes against upper_coverage_cutoff' and the column upper_cutoff_methylkit hold stats::quantile evaluated by the script on the rows methRead imported; the row 'scaling factor' compares max(median) / median with max(median) / median, both written in this script (lines 501 and 559). (b) The purpose texts of the extract table speak of 'the library median' (lines 189 to 191) while the column beside them is the median of the region over the median of the extract file (line 337). (c) lines_in_file holds the lines of the extract file in scope 'extract' (line 552) and of the whole file in scope 'full library' (line 439).

Given identical imported rows and identical medians, which are judged in rows of their own, these two rows cannot differ; what shows that methylKit applied the same cutoff and factor are the rows kept, the rows removed (39 rows with exactly the cutoff number of reads on the extract, 1,334 on the whole libraries) and the normalized counts.

result.verdict:
Accept. I found no wrong number and no judged comparison that cannot fail. The script /home/user/WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/06_diagnostics/check_methylkit_equivalence.R ran twice without error (about 8.8 minutes, 1.9 GB, one core) and wrote byte-identical tables, identical to the ones in the repository. Every group of numbers in its three tables was recomputed with code of my own (awk, Python, base R glm.fit) and agrees: the extract, the per-library filter facts, the united tables, the ties, the DML lists at all ten thresholds, the differences under the legacy coding, the six whole libraries, the step 05 tables inside the regions, the synthetic counts and the order of step 04. The header's statements about methylKit 1.28.0 (methRead, filterByCoverage, normalizeCoverage, unite, how logReg codes a factor and a character covariate, the legacy lines 143 to 150) agree with the installed source and the archived script. No style rule is broken (no em dash, no absolute path, no setwd, the treatment is called heat, set.seed precedes the only draws) and no data.table scoping mistake was found.

Three scratch copies with a deliberately altered helper show that the comparisons respond: the order of step 04 in the scaling and a kept first line give 38 rows DIFFERENT and the error at the end; first_line_lost() switched off is caught by the two I-38 rows; an upper filter with <= is caught too, but by a must() in part 7 that stops the script before any table is written and blames step 04. That failure path is the one finding I rate medium. The others are low: 45 unexplained (harmless) warnings in the log, the header argument of methylKit's route taken from a helper, three loose labels, part 5 weaker than it could be for corrected mode, one uncomputed sentence in the header, and one wrong percentage in the builder's report (86% to 87%, not 83% to 87%). The builder's proposed texts for the helper comment, I-05, I-38 and the README row agree with the tables.

What the script does not show, and does not claim: methylKit's own route on all 22 whole libraries (9 GB). Whole-file evidence is import and filter on six libraries; the first-line rule never reaches a united table because no first-line CpG has 10 reads in all libraries; in corrected mode the cutoffs of the extract (182 to 701) are far above those of the whole files (59 to 112), and 2,112 of the 9,201 CpGs compared there are ones step 05 does not test. My whole-file recount in Python closes the gap for the pipeline's own rule (480,579 and 454,555 CpGs, same sets, 0 of 31,718,214 and 0 of 30,000,630 counts different) and could be added to the script's extraction pass.

Nothing in the repository was changed. My logs, recount scripts and the scratch copies are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review-check_methylkit_equivalence/ (run1.log, run2.log, baseline.log, mutA.log, mutB.log, mutC.log; mine/extract.awk, recount_extract.py, order_step04.py, tables05.py, whole_tables.py and whole_tables.log, B_tests.R, B2_coding.R, C_synthetic.R, methylkit_source.txt).

issues_md_changes.current_text: - How much that skew matters was tested, with limits. A list confined to that run gives more terms below p = 0.01 than a random list of the same size, whatever the DML are. With every universe transcript of the accession run as the list of interest (11,284 of the 27,469 transcripts, no DML information), 1,041 of the 12,720 BP terms have p < 0.01, against a median of 52.5 for ten random lists of the same size (range 13 to 157), and nine of the ten legacy top BP terms for ploidy are among the 1,041. That check used one entry per transcript, not the line totals of the legacy test (I-43), and a list 18 times as long as the legacy list of 612 transcripts, so it does not separate the effect of position from the effect of list length. At the length of the legacy list, position alone about doubles the number of such terms and does not produce the legacy top terms: 200 random lists of 612 transcripts drawn from the run give a median of 72.5 BP terms with p < 0.01, against 38 for lists drawn from the whole universe, and in 171 of the 200 none of the ten legacy top terms has p < 0.01 (a single run by the agent that checked this paragraph; to be regenerated by `06_diagnostics/legacy_reader_mechanism.R`). The position skew is therefore a bias of the legacy test, not the explanation of its top terms, which is the isoform count of I-03.
issues_md_changes.proposed_text: - What that confinement does to the test was examined with an accession-run control, with limits (`06_diagnostics/legacy_reader_mechanism.R`, table `legacy_reader_position_control.csv`; 200 seeded random lists of each kind). Taken whole and with no DML information, the universe transcripts of the accession run (11,284 of the 27,469, in 5,264 genes) give 555 of the 12,720 BP terms with p < 0.01 when tested as step 09 tests, and 1,041 with one entry per transcript in place of the line totals of the legacy test (I-43). Random lists of 11,284 single transcripts give a median of 47 (range 8 to 287; 47.5 with one entry per transcript). That difference does not show an effect of position, because the run holds the isoforms of a gene together (every universe transcript of 4,562 of its 5,264 genes) and a list of single transcripts does not. Random gene sets with the run's numbers of genes and of transcripts per gene, and no common position, give a median of 763 terms (range 402 to 1,461; 189 of the 200 sets give at least 555) and 888 with one entry per transcript (598 to 1,240; 25 of the 200 give at least 1,041). The run lies within the range of such sets, so its excess over single transcripts is the isoform unit of I-03. Nine of the ten legacy top BP terms for ploidy have p < 0.01 in the test of the run (all but GO:0035561). That says little: the legacy list lies inside the run, six of the ten terms are annotated to the transcripts of a single gene each (`04_output/09_go_enrichment_legacy/tables/legacy_fisher_ploidy_BP.csv`, column `genes_annotated`), and in the random gene sets, which have nothing to do with the legacy list, the median is 4 of the ten (range 0 to 10). At the length of the legacy list (612 transcripts; the run is 18 times as long), lists of single transcripts confined to the run give no more terms than lists from the whole universe under the totals the legacy test used: the medians are 36 against 43.5, with 35.5 for lists drawn from the five linkage groups and 60 for lists drawn from 20 of the random gene sets (medians of the sets from 45 to 90). The transcripts of the run have more map lines each than those of the universe (19,855 lines for 9,277 transcripts with a BP term, 2.14 each, against 40,748 for 22,761, 1.79 each), and line totals count that against a list drawn from the run. With one entry per transcript the medians are 81 (run), 38 (universe), 48 (five linkage groups) and 64 (gene sets, 53.5 to 79): a list drawn from a part of the universe gives more terms than a list drawn from all of it, and most of the excess of the run appears for a random gene set of its size. In 175 of the 200 lists from the run (171 with one entry per transcript) none of the ten legacy top terms has p < 0.01. For lists of single transcripts, then, confinement to the run did not raise the number of terms under the totals of the legacy test, and it does not produce the legacy top terms, which rest on the isoform count of I-03. One limit remains: the lists of 612 are single transcripts, so none of them is a null distribution for the 383 terms of the legacy list (638 with one entry per transcript), which holds the isoforms of 168 genes; lists of isoform sets of that length were not drawn.

result.readme_row: | `legacy_reader_mechanism.R` | How the legacy enrichment script lost most of the ploidy annotation table and a quarter of the heat table: `read.table()` with its default quote characters, and apostrophes in GO term names. For the three legacy tables: rows, transcripts and genes returned by four reads (default quote characters, no quote character, the double quote alone, the apostrophe alone) with the warnings R gives; the lines with an unpaired apostrophe, the merged rows, and the proof by intervention; the transcripts and genes that vanish; where the survivors lie (accession run, linkage groups); the overlap with the universe gap; survival by number of transcripts per gene. For ploidy, an accession-run control of the BP test: every universe transcript of the surviving accession run as the list of interest, with no DML information, against random lists of single transcripts and against random gene sets with the run's numbers of genes and of transcripts per gene; and lists of the length of the legacy list drawn from the run, from the whole universe, from the linkage groups of the run and from 20 of the gene sets (5,000 seeded lists in all). Every list is tested with the totals counted in map lines (as step 09) and in transcripts. The run against single transcripts shows the isoform unit of I-03 together with the place of the run; the gene sets are the like-for-like comparison. Stops unless every read returns the rows predicted from the quote rule of `scan()` and its counts and p-values equal those of step 09. About 4 minutes, 1.3 GB; needs the outputs of steps 08 and 09 and GO.db 3.13.0 in the cache. Issues I-40, I-39, I-43, I-03. | `legacy_reader_mechanism.csv` (long format: table, quantity, value, definition), `legacy_reader_by_linkage_group.csv`, `legacy_reader_position_control.csv` (the accession-run control) |
result.notes:
All five review findings were checked with my own code, found right, and applied. The script ran clean twice from the repository root (237 s and 235 s, peak memory 1.30 GB) and the three CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs. Every target of parts (a) to (f) still holds exactly.

One result differs from the reviewer's, and it matters for the issue text. The reviewer's random gene sets are all whole genes, but the run holds 702 of its 5,264 genes only in part. Matched exactly, random gene sets give a median of 888 terms with transcript totals (run 1,041; 25 of 200 sets reach it) and 763 with line totals (run 555; 189 of 200). The reviewer had 1,072.5 and 963, which I reproduced exactly before changing the match. The reading of finding 1 stands: the excess of the run over single transcripts (47) is the isoform unit, and the run lies within the range of gene sets with no common position. The handoff (07_documentation/session_handoff.md, the two paragraphs on this script) quotes the reviewer's 1,072.5 and 963 and the builder's proposed text; both are superseded.

At the length of the legacy list the picture is less clean than either earlier text said:
- Line totals, as the legacy test: run 36, universe 43.5, five linkage groups 35.5, random gene sets 60 (set medians 45 to 90). The run lies below all 20 sets.
- Transcript totals: run 81, universe 38, five linkage groups 48, random gene sets 64 (53.5 to 79). The run lies just above all 20 sets.
So most of the excess of run lists appears for any gene set of that size, but I would not write that position adds nothing. The proposed I-40 text says only what the table supports.

Checks behind the new code, all in scratch:
- The 200 gene sets have the structure of the run by a second method (data.table grouping).
- An explicit gene-by-gene version of the draw under another seed gives the same distribution (medians 770 and 890.5).
- topGO itself, called as step 09 calls it, gives bit-identical p-values for five of the new lists in both units.
- Every summary column of the control table was recomputed with base R from the per-list results: no mismatch in 16 rows.
- Three altered copies stop with a plain message and write nothing: halves that do not match the run, one wrong p-value in the step 09 table (the old all.equal check lets it pass), and wrongly dealt gene sets.

Limits and things not done:
- A median of 200 lists has a bootstrap standard error of about 2 to 4 terms (12 to 19 for the gene sets), so differences of a few terms between kinds mean nothing. This number is from scratch, not from the script, and is not in the proposed issue text.
- The lists of 612 are single transcripts. A control with random isoform sets of the legacy size (168 genes), from the run and from the universe, would be the direct null for the 383 terms. The review did not ask for it and I did not add it.
- The reviewer's comparison with other accession windows is not in the script.
- The output file keeps the name legacy_reader_position_control.csv because the specification names it; the header says what the word stands for.
- Only R 4.3.3 was available.

No file was removed from 06_diagnostics: the script writes the same three files. I edited no README, helper, pipeline script, run_config.R or issues.md and ran no state-changing git command. The parent session's snapshot commit 7251365 already holds the final script and tables (same md5 as on disk), though its message says not final. The run line of 06_diagnostics/README.md still says review pending; a fitting comment is "about 4 minutes; after steps 08 and 09".

Scratch work, including the reviewer-design reproduction and the three failure tests, is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/fix-legacy_reader_mechanism.

changes_made: Finding 1 (medium, Monte Carlo error of the label permutation), applied by complete enumeration: comparison 8 now evaluates every labelling of the ploidy labels within cohort instead of 1,000 draws. That is 252 x 924 = 232,848 labellings, of which 110,880 are also balanced on the acute heat shock (one of each mirror pair is computed; the script checks both totals against the binomial coefficients). Exact for both schemes, with no seed: CpGs called per labelling (median, 5th and 95th percentile, smallest, largest, number and share of labellings reaching the real number), share of eligible CpGs called by 5-point and 10-point methylation bin and inside and outside each track, and the median, 2.5th and 97.5th percentile of the odds ratio against eligible CpGs per track with the share of labellings at or above the real value.

Estimator for the labellings: the odds ratio of a labelling is the cross-product ratio (a d / b c). fisher.test for about 815,000 tables per mode is not feasible, and its absolute tolerance is coarse for the small odds ratios that some labellings give. feature_odds_label_permutation.csv has a new column odds_ratio_real_cross_product beside odds_ratio_real (they differ by at most 1 in the fourth decimal), and the share at or above the real value compares cross-product ratios on both sides.

The 1,000 random labellings per scheme (same seed 20261119, same draws as before) are kept only for comparison 3 under shuffled labels, which needs the SD and its deciles again for every labelling. New columns give the 95% Monte Carlo range of the median, of the 2.5th and of the 97.5th percentile (order statistics, function quantile_mc_range) and the standard error of the share. The notes column says that a difference between the two schemes inside those ranges is sampling error. matched_n_permutations (1,000) is now separate from n_permutations (232,848 or 110,880).

New checks inside the script: each of the 2,000 random labellings is looked up in the enumeration and the script stops unless all 16 counts agree (this also guards the pruning of the enumeration); the row of the real labelling must equal the list of the whole-number rule; the labelling with the ploidy labels exchanged in one cohort must give the count computed directly.

Method of the enumeration: candidates are the CpGs whose per-library percentages span more than the threshold; they are processed 8,000 at a time; for each choice of labels in the first cohort a CpG is evaluated over the 924 choices of the second cohort only if a bound computed on whole numbers allows a call (about 15% of the candidate rows in legacy mode). About 70 seconds per mode.

Finding 2 (low, resampling error of the block intervals): n_boot raised from 2,000 to 10,000 (same seed; the first 2,000 resamples are those of the earlier version). The notes column of every block row now gives the 95% range of each end from order statistics. To hold memory, the weights are filled in place, and a cell held by more than a tenth of the blocks is multiplied without copying its weights (identical counts, whole numbers).

Finding 3 (low, decile cuts): SD deciles are now groups of equal size by rank among the eligible CpGs, ties in row order (function rank_group), in comparison 3 and in the code for shuffled labels. A DML outside the eligible range gets the decile of the eligible CpG next below it in SD. The check that both code paths agree for the real labels is tightened from 1e-3 to 1e-9 and stops with a message. sd_from and sd_to of the SD table are now the smallest and largest SD among the eligible CpGs of the group.

Finding 4 (low, ties at the threshold): the stored-difference rule of step 05 and the whole-number rule of the script are compared at every CpG that is not an exact tie. The counts table has three new rows per contrast and mode: exact ties, ties that step 05 counted as above the threshold, CpGs called by the whole-number rule. Result: heat has one exact tie in both modes (NW_022994958.1:20934), not called by step 05; ploidy has none. The header says how step 05 treats ties. The labellings are compared with the list that the whole-number rule calls under the real labels, and the script requires the threshold to be a whole number.
Finding 5 (low): in the counts table only values that are not whole numbers are rounded to six significant digits.
Finding 6 (low, precision of fisher.test): no change of method or of digits. The header and the estimate_method column now state the tolerance of the root search (about 0.0001).

Finding 7 (low, comparison 4): each range is written twice, labelled 'every DML of the list' (as before; the notes give the number of DML outside) and 'DML inside the range only' (56 new rows; for 15% to 85% in legacy mode gene body 2.2274 and 1.8884).

Header rewritten for all of the above (run time about 10 minutes, about 2.1 GB). Effect on the files: feature_odds_matched.csv has 320 rows (264 before). The 152 rows of comparisons 1, 2, 5, 6 and of comparison 4 with every DML are identical to before. Comparison 3 is identical in legacy mode; in corrected mode 5 of its 14 rows change in the fourth decimal, because three CpGs change decile. All block rows changed (10,000 resamples). The SD table is unchanged in legacy mode apart from sd_from and sd_to. The matched columns of the permutation table are identical to before in legacy mode.
findings_not_applied: All seven findings were checked, found right and applied; none was rejected. Where the review offered two fixes, the alternatives below were not taken.

Finding 1, alternative 'keep the draws and write intervals beside them': used only for the matched odds ratios (comparison 3 under shuffled labels). A complete enumeration of those would need the SD and its deciles for 116,424 labellings per mode, about an hour per mode at 25 to 30 ms each.

Finding 1, estimator: the enumeration writes cross-product ratios for the labellings, not fisher.test estimates. In scratch the cross-product ratio stayed within 0.04% of the conditional estimate solved at high precision for tables of this kind, while fisher.test itself was off by several percent for odds ratios below 0.001. For the real list the two agree to the fourth decimal.

Finding 2, alternative 'write block intervals to 2 decimals': not applied. The number of resamples was raised instead and the resampling range of each end is in the notes column. All odds columns keep four decimals so that the table has one format.

Finding 4, window of 1e-9: not used. The whole-number rule identifies exact ties, so the two rules are compared at every CpG that is not an exact tie, which is the sharper check. In these data the nearest non-tie is 0.0014 points from the threshold and the largest total coverage of a CpG is 115,301 reads, so rounding cannot move a non-tie across the threshold.

Finding 6, alternative 'write 3 significant digits': not applied, so that the rows stay comparable with step 07 digit for digit. The tolerance is stated in the header and in the estimate_method column instead.

result.readme_row: | `feature_odds_matched.R` | Are DML more likely than comparable CpGs to lie in gene bodies, CDS, introns, exon UTR, lncRNA, transposable elements or intergenic sequence? Repeats the odds ratios of step 07 and stops if they differ; then compares DML with eligible CpGs of the same 5-point methylation bin, of the same bin and decile of within-group SD, with other ranges of mean methylation (5% to 95%, 15% to 85%; with every DML and with the DML inside the range only), by coverage quartile (transposable elements) and CDS against intron; adds intervals from a bootstrap over 100 kb blocks (10,000 resamples; the resampling error of each end is in the notes column). For ploidy it evaluates every labelling of the ploidy labels within cohort (232,848; 110,880 of them also balanced on the acute heat shock): number of CpGs called, share called by methylation bin and by track, and the odds ratios against eligible CpGs, all without sampling error; the matched odds ratios are given for 1,000 random labellings per scheme with their Monte Carlo ranges. The permutation applies the difference rule only; no permutation exists for heat. Both modes. About 10 minutes, 2.1 GB. Issues I-41 and I-06. Written by an agent, reviewed by an independent agent that reproduced its numbers with code of its own, and revised after that review | `feature_odds_matched.csv`, `feature_odds_matched_within_group_sd.csv`, `feature_odds_label_permutation.csv`, `feature_odds_label_permutation_counts.csv` |
result.notes:
Final runs. The script was run twice from the repository root (WGBS_CACHE_DIR set, WGBS_CORES=1): exit 0 both times, 618 s and 630 s, peak resident memory 2,053 and 2,072 MB, one thread, empty stderr. The four CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs (md5: feature_odds_matched.csv 4fba4dac..., within_group_sd 7dbb04aa..., label_permutation 12a6f17a..., label_permutation_counts bff59413...) and are the copies now in 06_diagnostics/. No output file had to be removed: the script writes the same four files as before. I ran no git command that changes state; a snapshot commit of the main session (a6e0a1b) already holds the revised script, and the four CSV files show as modified.

Cost of the fixes. Run time rose from about 4 to about 10 minutes and peak memory from about 1.4 to about 2.1 GB (limit 3 GB). The 10,000 block resamples take about 3 minutes per mode, the enumeration about 70 seconds per mode. The first full development run peaked at 2.9 GB; the enumeration in slices and the handling of the resampling weights brought it down.

Departure from the task text. The task asked for 1,000 permutations with a fixed seed. Counts, shares and the odds ratios against eligible CpGs now cover all labellings instead, as the review proposed; the 1,000 random labellings per scheme remain for the matched odds ratios only. The rows of the counts table keep their names ("CpGs called per permutation, median" and so on), but the row "permutations" now reads 232,848 or 110,880.

One fault of my own, repaired before the final runs: a product of two integer counts overflowed in the first draft and gave NA shares with a warning. The final runs have no warning.

Checks outside the script (scratch, not reproducible from the repository): (1) two prototype enumerations with different pruning gave counts identical to each other for all 116,424 x 16 cells and reproduce the reviewer's enumeration in every figure quoted in the review, in both modes; (2) an independent block bootstrap with the script's seed reproduces 0.7625 to 1.7888 and 0.7621 to 1.3582, and its first 2,000 resamples reproduce the earlier 0.7725 to 1.8228; (3) three mutated copies (bound too strict, wrong row index, mirror image handled wrongly) all stop at a check; (4) my own recomputation confirmed findings 3, 4, 6 and 7 before I changed anything (four whole quantile indices in corrected mode and three CpGs that change decile; one exact heat tie stored as exactly 20; fisher.test off by up to 3.9e-5 relative; 2.2274 and 1.8884 for DML inside 15% to 85%).

For the analyst. (a) The block bootstrap of the script's seed sits slightly high: 50,000 resamples in scratch give 0.75 to 1.77 for the matched ploidy gene-body interval and 0.76 to 1.36 for heat, so 0.76 to 1.79 should be quoted with its resampling range. (b) I-06 item 5 says "40 of the 252 regroupings of the heat cohort do (median 754)"; my scratch enumeration gives 40 of 252 and a median of 753.5, and confirms 903 of 924 with median 1,530. The script does not write these, so they are not in issues_md_changes. (c) The same superseded numbers stand outside issues.md: 07_documentation/reproducibility_plan.md, decision 11 ("median 2.7", "1.18 after the same matching") and 07_documentation/session_handoff.md lines 74 and 79 (2.61, 55%, 0.77 to 1.82, 0.37%). (d) Corrected mode, not in the task targets: matched gene body 1.24 (block interval 0.85 to 1.96) and 0.94 (0.72 to 1.26); 708 CpGs called at the median (484 to 1,327), 34,656 labellings (14.9%) at or above 952; gene-body odds ratio under shuffled labels 3.11 (2.02 to 5.12), real 2.85 reached in 66.1%.

Scratch directory: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/fix-feature_odds_matched (baseline/ holds the files before the fix, run1/ and run2/ the logs and outputs of the final runs, work/ the check scripts).

issues_md_changes.proposed_text: The rows are rows of `06_diagnostics/coverage_filter_variants.csv`, written by `06_diagnostics/coverage_filter_variants.R`; the cutoffs of each library and the pooled cutoff are in `06_diagnostics/coverage_filter_cutoffs.csv`. The DML counts of the alternative rows are the legacy DML at retained CpGs. They are the lists that step 05 would report under each alternative, for two reasons that the script checks. First, no alternative filter changes the median coverage of a library (column `libraries_with_changed_median`), so the scaling factors, and with them the p-value and the difference of every retained CpG, are those of legacy mode. Second, q-values estimated again with methylKit's SLIM function on the retained CpGs of each alternative give the same lists, locus for locus (column `lists_same_with_reestimated_q`). The first reason is a fact of these data and has a small margin in one library: zr3644_3 keeps its median coverage as long as it loses no more than 12,102 of its most covered CpGs, and the filter of the second row takes 10,409 of them (the filter of the first row 8,810; columns `n_removable_before_median_changes`, `n_removed_base_1` and `n_removed_base_2` of `coverage_filter_cutoffs.csv`). For zr3644_14 the largest removal is just under half of the margin (9,786 of 19,667), and for the other 20 libraries it is at most a fifth. result.readme_row: | `coverage_filter_variants.R` | How far the CpG and DML counts depend on how the upper coverage filter of the Methods is read (I-05). From the 22 coverage files: the 99.9th percentile cutoff of each library with the percentile taken over CpGs with at least 1, 2 or 10 reads, and one pooled cutoff; nine filter rules applied to the CpGs of legacy mode, with the CpGs kept and the legacy DML at kept CpGs; what the rule of corrected mode removes (number of libraries at the cutoff, repeat track, mitochondrial sequence, unplaced scaffolds, runs of removed CpGs with a reference from 1,000 seeded random draws); and whether those DML counts are what step 05 would report under each rule (q-value rule in the step 05 tables; library medians under each rule, and how many of its most covered CpGs each library can lose before its median changes; q-values estimated again with methylKit's SLIM function). Stops unless the rule of corrected mode gives the CpGs and DML lists of step 05. The base of corrected mode follows `import_min_coverage` of `run_config.R`. 6 to 7 minutes, 1.6 GB, one core; needs the coverage files in the cache. | `coverage_filter_variants.csv` (one row per rule), `coverage_filter_cutoffs.csv` (one row per library), `coverage_filter_removed_cpgs.csv` (one row per set of CpGs), `coverage_filter_qvalue_rule.csv` (one row per set of CpGs and contrast) |
result.notes:
All four review findings were right and all four are applied; none is left out. The script is final: two runs from the repository root exited with status 0 and no warning (352 s and 347 s, peak 1.6 GB, one core), the four CSV files are byte-identical between them, and all 22 targets agree.

What the fix of finding 1 was tested on. I could not rerun steps 04 and 05 with another import threshold, so the runs below use corrected-mode tables that I rebuilt from the legacy tables for base 1 and base 10. That is valid for a test because no library median changes under those filters, so only the q-values and the lists are new. They show that the script runs under those settings, not what step 05 would write.
- `import_min_coverage = 1`: runs to the end. The rule of corrected mode is then base 1 (451,328 CpGs; 949, 2,267, 159) and the pooled cutoff is 84 reads.
- `import_min_coverage = 10`: runs to the end. The rule of corrected mode is base 10 (469,453; 959, 2,292, 159) and the pooled cutoff is 134 reads.
- `import_min_coverage = 1` with the real tables of step 05 (base 2): stops after the pass over the files with the message that names the setting, and writes nothing.
Both complete runs were repeated with the final script and gave identical tables.

Other checks of the new code, all in the scratch folder:
- The margin equals a brute-force count on 400 random sets of small libraries, and equals the reviewer's values (zr3644_3 12,102; zr3644_14 19,667).
- With artificially low bounds, where 4 to 21 medians do change, the margin and the direct comparison of medians agree library by library.
- The rounding function stops on a real fourth decimal and on a cutoff a hair away from a whole number.
- The new stop for line 1 and the guard of section 5 fire when their condition is altered.

Three small additions go beyond the suggested fixes and can be taken out without touching anything else: the setting named in one stop message, the stopifnot that ties the margin to the changed medians, and the second condition on rounding.

Left as it was:
- The header says "about 7 minutes"; seven measured runs took 5.8 to 5.9 minutes. The review did not raise it.
- Peak memory was 1.77 GB in the two scratch runs with another threshold, against 1.6 GB with the committed config.

The two must() calls are now judged rows, so a disagreement between the routes reaches part 8, the three tables are written, and the script then lists the failing comparisons and stops. The purpose texts now rest on the column beside them (mitochondrial sequence 8.7 to 99, NW_022994810.1 6 to 11.33).
Finding 4c (lines_in_file held two different things): column renamed lines_read, with a header note that it is the extract file in scope 'extract' and the whole coverage file in scope 'full library'.

Finding 5 (part 5 weaker than it could be), both parts of the suggested fix. findings_not_applied: Finding 7 (the builder's report says 83% to 87% of p-values are not bit-identical under the legacy coding): right, but nothing in the script or its tables carries the figure, so there is nothing to change in the code. The share is 86% to 87% (8,346 and 8,410 of 9,642; 7,954 and 7,973 of 9,201); that figure is used in this report.

Finding 6, the alternative of counting the CpGs behind the glm.fit warnings: not taken. The warnings are raised inside calculateDiffMeth, so the handler cannot name the CpG without refitting every CpG outside methylKit; the review offered the removal of the sentence as an equal fix, and that is what was done.

Finding 2, the alternative of not calling getMethylDiff where no CpG passes: not taken, because the selection at those thresholds would then no longer be methylKit's own; the warnings are collected and logged instead.

It checks the script's reading of methylKit's source (an input), its message names methylKit, and the review did not name it. result.readme_row: | `check_methylkit_equivalence.R` | Shows that the low-memory import of step 05 (`02_R_functions/methylkit_helpers.R`) gives what methylKit's own `methRead`, `filterByCoverage`, `normalizeCoverage` and `unite` give, in both modes (issues I-05, I-38). Both routes run on a regional extract of all 22 coverage files that keeps the first line of every file (2.0% of the CpGs tested in legacy mode, 1.6% in corrected mode): the same rows imported, kept and removed and the same normalized counts in every library, identical united tables (9,642 and 9,201 CpGs), and identical differences, p-values, q-values and DML lists for both contrasts. Also compared: import and filter on six whole libraries, with methylKit and with the records of step 05 (22.8 million kept rows, none differs); every count of the two tables of step 05 with the raw counts of the 22 whole files (31.7 and 30.0 million values, none differs), and the CpGs of those tables inside the regions with the rule of each mode; rounding on synthetic counts with exact ties. Recorded, not judged: p-values under the covariate coding of the legacy script (within 2e-8, relative; same DML lists), and the order of operations of step 04 (at most 25 of 3.3 million scaled counts of the extract differ; correlations change by less than 1e-5). If a comparison that must agree does not, the tables are written and the script then stops with an error. About 9 minutes, 2.2 GB, one core; needs the coverage files and the tables of step 05. Written by an agent and reviewed by an independent agent, which recomputed every group of numbers with code of its own; its findings are applied | `check_methylkit_equivalence.csv` (one row per comparison), `check_methylkit_equivalence_libraries.csv` (one row per library, mode and scope), `check_methylkit_equivalence_extract.csv` (one row per region of the extract) |
result.notes:
All seven review findings were checked and found right; six are applied to the script and the seventh concerns only the builder's report. The final script ran twice from the repository root (516 s and 518 s, peak 2,159 MB, exit status 0) with byte-identical tables: 121 comparisons, 94 identical, 1 within tolerance, 26 recorded, none different.

What changed in the tables: 103 of the 112 earlier rows are unchanged to the byte; 9 are renamed with the same values (finding 4a, and the part 'tables of step 05'); 9 rows are new (the three former stop conditions as judged rows, the rule set inside the regions per mode, the whole-table counts per mode). The library table has the same values under three new column names; the extract table differs only in the two ratio columns, now relative to the whole-file median.

Checks outside the script:
- Failure path: one run of the unchanged final script in a scratch copy of the project with altered helpers and altered tables of step 05 (see targets). It ends with exit status 1 after writing its tables there; nothing in the repository was touched.
- New numbers recounted in Python with no shared code: whole-table counts and tie counts, the rule sets inside the regions, the nine pairs of ratio values of the extract table. All equal.

Not verified by me: the reviewer's recounts of the unchanged rows (I rely on the rows being byte-identical to the reviewed ones), and the import at mincov = 1 behind the I-38 Evidence sentence.

Reported, not fixed (01_pipeline/04_cpg_coverage.R, function percent_methylation): step 04 computes round(new_cov * nc / cv) where methylKit computes round(new_cov * (nc / cv)). Size on the extract: see the target row. Fix when step 04 is next touched: call scale_counts_like_methylkit(cv, nc, cv - nc, sc[j]).

What the script still does not show: methylKit's own route on all 22 whole libraries at once (about 9 GB). Whole-file evidence is import and filter on six libraries plus, since this fix, every count of the two tables of step 05 against the 22 whole files. Which CpGs each mode keeps on the whole files is checked by coverage_filter_variants.R (it stops unless its sets are the CpGs of step 05; I read that check in its current state). On the extract the corrected-mode cutoffs are 182 to 701 reads against 59 to 112 on the whole files.
